Q: With ArchUnit, how can I make sure that all classes in my project are starting with the same package? A:

You can use the simple rule

classes().should().resideInAPackage( /* e.g. */ "com.tngtech.archunit..")

The parameter defines a PackageMatcher, where .. stands for any sequence of packages, including zero packages.

Make sure to import all classes of interest for your ArchUnit test (most conveniently using JUnit support).

Q: Set daemonset environment variable value based on node label value A:

This approach won't work and you'll need to change your code to get the information a different way.

There's a specific set of fields available through the downward API. All of these are fields available on the Pod object. You can inject spec.nodeName because the scheduler fills in that field on the Pod, but you can't use this mechanism to inject information about the Node or get metadata off of the Node object.

You might put whatever information you need in a file on disk and use a hostPath: type volume to retrieve it. Another option could be to store a JSON file or some other file format that supports dictionary-type objects in a ConfigMap and decode that at startup time.

Q: Making Material segmented buttons align without cutting off text A:

I have try to find something to work using your suggestions and experience.
And I find this solution:

1. add Modifier.height(IntrinsicSize.Max) to parent

SingleChoiceSegmentedButtonRow(
    modifier = Modifier.height(IntrinsicSize.Max)
) {
    ...
}

2. add Modifier.FillMaxHeight() to childs

...
        SegmentedButton(
            modifier = Modifier.fillMaxHeight(),
            ...
        ) {
            ...
        }
...

3. add \n to split long string to separate lines

...
    val options = listOf("Short here", "Two words", "Longer\nWords")
...

I think that "cut off" problem is because composable do not count text moved to another line as separate line.

Q: Algorithms for selecting 3D elements (vertices, edges, faces) under a 2D rectangle region A:

To select certain parts of a model by dragging a rectangle in a 3D viewport, the 3D points of the model are converted to 2D screen locations. This allows the software to identify where parts of the model appear on-screen so that they can be selected correctly.

Vertex Selection:

All vertices that appear within the rectangle will be selected by the software.

Edge Selection:

If one or more vertices of an edge are located within the rectangle or if the edge intersects the rectangle, then that edge is considered to be selected.

Face Selection:

For a face to be selected, the projected area of that face must overlap with the rectangle. For triangular faces, you can either perform simple math calculations for the selection area or use bounding boxes to check if they intersect the selection area.

When working with large models, performance can be improved using techniques such as bounding box selection, octree selection, and GPU selection.

Many software solutions support these selection techniques including Autodesk; Siemens Digital Industries Software; Dassault Systèmes; MecSoft Corporation; Unity Technologies; and Epic Games.

Q: LossySetItemError when converting column type of 'int64' to 'float64' with astype() A:

Try to avoid .loc for type conversion. Assigning directly to the column name tells Pandas to replace the entire Series/pointer rather than trying to update the values within the existing block.

Instead of: df.loc[:, 'col'] = df['col'].astype('float64')

Try to use: df['col'] = df['col'].astype('float64')
